entities.summary:
Mirza Yusuf (1450-1469) was the last sultan of the Qara Qoyunlu, also known as the Black Sheep Turkomans, to have significant authority. His rule was marked by attempts to expand the empire's borders and strengthen its military power.

Born in unknown circumstances, Mirza Yusuf rose to prominence within the Qara Qoyunlu clan and eventually succeeded his father, Sultan Shahrukh, as the ruler of the empire in 1468. However, his reign was cut short when he died on October 31, 1469, at the age of around 19.

Mirza Yusuf's legacy is complex and multifaceted. On the one hand, he played a crucial role in maintaining the empire's territorial integrity during a time of great turmoil in the region. On the other hand, his inability to secure a lasting peace with neighboring powers ultimately led to the decline of the Qara Qoyunlu empire.

Mirza Yusuf's death marked the beginning of a new era for the Turkomans, as the empire was eventually fragmented and its territories absorbed by other regional powers. Nevertheless, his impact on the history of the region cannot be overstated, and he remains an important figure in the annals of Turkoman history.

Mirza Yusuf's story is also significant because it highlights the challenges faced by young leaders in maintaining power and stability in a rapidly changing world. His tragic fate serves as a reminder of the fragility of human life and the importance of effective leadership in times of turmoil.
